name: plains
prompt:
Create production-quality composable terrain sprite sheet for a procedural dark-fantasy regional atlas in a phone landscape strategy game.
VIEW: old Tolkien-style illustrated map relief, slightly raised north-facing view, coherent lighting from upper left; not isometric cubes. Fine hand-engraved hatching interpreted as crisp pixel clusters with rich small-scale detail. Muted Elden Ring map palette: parchment ochre, desaturated olive, grey peat, reddish umber rock, charcoal shadows. Original artwork.
OUTPUT: transparent background, NO text, NO labels, NO grid lines, NO frame, NO paper rectangles, no buildings or characters. Every sprite separate with generous transparent gutters; contain full silhouette within its equally spaced cell. Ground feet dissolve into scattered fine stones/grass so pieces can overlap without rectangular seams. Small forms read as terrain masses, not oversized individual plants. Exactly the specified rectangular grid, all cells occupied, consistent scale and camera. Detailed drawable source art, not a screenshot or UI.
GRID: exactly 4 columns and 3 rows (12 sprites), landscape image.
SUBJECT: Rolling dry grassland. 12 distinct connected landscape fragments: low continuous grassy ridge, ridge with saddle, forked ridge, ridge ending in rocky knoll, long hedgerow with tiny shrubs, curved hedgerow, hedgerow gap, long eroded gully, gully bend, gully mouth with gravel, clustered meadow hummocks, rough grassy bank. Warm ochre, umber ink, muted olive grass. No yellow pyramid hills.
Arrange the 12 listed fragments left-to-right, top-to-bottom.
